scenes.title: Performance Tuning & Throughput
scenes.subtitle: Squeezing maximum throughput from Kafka
scenes.narration: Tuning Kafka for throughput means balancing batching, compression, and parallelism against the latency your use case can tolerate.

scenes.title: Producer Levers
bullets: batch.size groups records into larger sends
linger.ms waits briefly to fill batches
compression.type shrinks payloads on the wire
scenes.narration: On the producer side, batch.size controls how many bytes are grouped into a single request. linger.ms tells the producer to wait a few milliseconds so batches fill up before sending, trading a little latency for much higher throughput. Compression such as lz4 or zstd shrinks payloads on the wire and on disk. And buffer.memory sets how much data the producer can hold during bursts before it must block.

scenes.title: Consumer and Broker Levers
bullets: fetch.min.bytes lets consumers pull bigger batches
More partitions unlock more consumer parallelism
Sized page cache serves reads without disk I/O
Match partition count to broker and disk capacity
scenes.narration: On the consumer side, fetch.min.bytes lets a consumer wait for a larger batch, improving efficiency at a small latency cost. Adding partitions unlocks more consumer parallelism, since each partition feeds one consumer in a group. Brokers rely heavily on the operating system page cache to serve reads without hitting disk. And you should match partition counts to your broker and disk capacity, since too many partitions add overhead.

scenes.title: The Throughput Trade-off
scenes.narration: The central tension is throughput versus latency. Increasing batch size and linger produces larger, less frequent requests. That amortizes overhead and drives throughput up. The cost is a small increase in end-to-end latency, so you tune these knobs to the tolerance of your application.

scenes.title: A High-Throughput Producer
scenes.code:
producer = Producer({
    'bootstrap.servers': 'localhost:9092',
    'batch.size': 262144,        # 256 KB batches
    'linger.ms': 20,             # wait to fill batches
    'compression.type': 'zstd',  # strong compression
    'acks': 'all',
    'enable.idempotence': True,
})
scenes.narration: This configuration targets high throughput. Larger 256-kilobyte batches and a 20-millisecond linger let the producer send fewer, fuller requests. Zstandard compression cuts network and storage cost significantly. Keeping acks all with idempotence means you gain throughput without sacrificing durability or introducing duplicates.

scenes.text: Measure before and after every change. Benchmark with your real payloads, tune one lever at a time, and stop when you hit your latency budget.
scenes.narration: The golden rule of tuning is to measure before and after every change. Benchmark with your real payloads, tune one lever at a time, and stop once you hit your latency budget.
